plan.change: Prebuild and regression-test the future base-owned trusted registry transition enforcement executor.
expectedChanges: Add base-owned validation of candidate registry transitions before static success can be returned.
Require the candidate registry contract path set to exactly equal the base-owned contract path set.

Allow only steady-to-pending authorization of one existing contract where base expectedBlob equals fromBlob, candidate expectedBlob equals toBlob, all unrelated contracts and definitions are unchanged, and the candidate contracted file still equals fromBlob.
Allow a pending base registry to remain unchanged while the preauthorized contracted file transitions to toBlob.
Allow pending-to-steady cleanup only after the contracted file equals toBlob and without other registry definition changes.

Reject contract deletion/addition, executor-kind changes, check-set changes, unrelated expectedBlob drift, malformed transition metadata, same-PR target-file change during authorization, and retargeting of an existing pending transition.
Expose trusted registry-transition evidence without logging raw candidate registry JSON.
Add adversarial tests for the transition state machine.
Do not open or merge this prebuild branch; use the tested executor Git blob only after a separate base-owned registry authorization package.
hqDecisions: This branch is prebuild-only and must not be merged before its executor blob is preauthorized by a separate registry-only package.
Trusted runtime authorization continues to come only from the PR-base registry.
Candidate registry data may be parsed and validated as inert data but never used for executor dispatch in the same PR.
plan.manualCheckExemptionReason: Prebuild-only branch; candidate regression tests are used to prove the future executor before exact-blob authorization.
plan.rollback: Discard the prebuild branch. Do not merge it directly.
unverified: This prebuild is not trusted until its exact executor blob is authorized in the base registry and transitioned through a fresh PR.
plan.problem: Candidate-owned regression tests cannot protect the registry contract set. The base-owned executor must validate candidate registry transitions as data.
plan.currentContract: The trusted executor loads the PR-base registry for dispatch and exact-blob checks but does not validate candidate registry edits before they can become the next trusted base.
plan.whyExistingIsInsufficient: A registry-only PR can remove a contract while old base-owned exact-blob checks still pass because no contracted file changed.
plan.design: Parse the candidate registry as canonical inert JSON using base-owned validation, compare it to the loaded base registry, and produce an independent registryTransition result. Unchanged candidate registry is accepted. A steady base may authorize exactly one existing contract by changing only its expectedBlob from fromBlob to toBlob and setting canonical pending metadata while the candidate target file remains fromBlob. A pending base may be used unchanged while the file moves to toBlob, then a later registry-only cleanup may return to steady only when the file is already toBlob. staticOk must be false for any invalid registry transition regardless of Plan staticChecks.
alternativesRejected: Rely on candidate tests or hardcoded candidate constants; the candidate can modify both.
Allow arbitrary authorized blob arrays; this widens the trust window unnecessarily.
Self-contract the registry file; this creates an update deadlock.
Use candidate registry definitions for current-PR dispatch; this breaks the base-owned trust boundary.
plan.migration: After prebuild tests pass, compute the future executor Git blob. A separate registry-only authorization PR will preauthorize that blob. A fresh executor-only transition PR will then install this exact file while leaving the pending registry unchanged. A cleanup PR under the new executor will return the registry to steady.
plan.compatibility: Existing static check IDs, evidence schema, required status names, node-syntax behavior, and exact contracted-file enforcement remain in place. The new registryTransition evidence is additive and invalid transitions only tighten staticOk.
boundaryCases: steady to pending may change exactly one existing contract expectedBlob and transition metadata only.
Authorization PR must leave the contracted target file at fromBlob.
Any unrelated contract object change is rejected.
pending base with unchanged candidate registry can accompany exact file transition to toBlob.
pending to steady is accepted only when the target file already equals toBlob and all contract definitions remain unchanged.
pending retargeting or pending to a different pending transition is rejected.
Invalid transition makes staticOk false even if requested static checks otherwise pass.
testPlan: Run Change Operations Tests on this prebuild branch.
Verify valid steady-to-pending authorization passes while target file remains fromBlob.
Verify same-PR target file change during authorization fails.
Verify unrelated contract or check-definition changes fail.
Verify pending unchanged plus exact toBlob file transition passes.
Verify valid pending-to-steady cleanup passes only after target file equals toBlob.
Verify malformed or retargeted pending transitions fail.
Use the resulting exact executor blob only in a later fresh authorization/transition sequence.
